question.prompt: Name a famous line from a space-based sci-fi film or TV series that fans still quote.
question.criteria: Any recognizable quoted line spoken in a released space-based science-fiction film or TV series counts; minor wording and punctuation variations are accepted.

answers.canonical: May the Force be with you
aliases: May the force be with u
answers.evidence: This blessing is spoken throughout the Star Wars films.
This Vulcan farewell is associated with Spock in Star Trek.
Admiral Ackbar exclaims this during the space battle in Return of the Jedi.
This declaration is associated with the Borg in Star Trek.
This creed is repeatedly spoken by Mandalorians in The Mandalorian.
Han Solo says this to C-3PO in The Empire Strikes Back.
Captain Jean-Luc Picard frequently gives this command in Star Trek: The Next Generation.
Hudson exclaims this in Aliens.
This is the catchphrase of Commander Peter Quincy Taggart in Galaxy Quest.
This oath is associated with Dr. Lazarus in Galaxy Quest.
This communal affirmation recurs in the reimagined Battlestar Galactica.

answers.canonical: I am a leaf on the wind
aliases: I'm a leaf on the wind
I am a leaf on the wind, watch how I soar
answers.evidence: Wash says this while piloting in Serenity.
Darth Vader says this to Luke Skywalker in The Empire Strikes Back.

answers.canonical: I have a bad feeling about this
aliases: I've got a bad feeling about this
answers.evidence: Variations of this line recur across the Star Wars films.
Captain Jean-Luc Picard uses this command to set his ship underway in Star Trek: The Next Generation.

answers.canonical: Open the pod bay doors, HAL
answers.evidence: Dave Bowman gives HAL this instruction in 2001: A Space Odyssey.
Picard defiantly shouts this in the Star Trek: The Next Generation episode Chain of Command, Part II.
Starbuck gives this response to Adama's recurring greeting in the reimagined Battlestar Galactica.
Groot repeatedly uses this phrase in the Guardians of the Galaxy films.

aliases: Smoke me a kipper, I'll be back for breakfast
answers.evidence: Ace Rimmer uses this catchphrase in Red Dwarf.

question.explanation: Space sci-fi has supplied fans with everything from Jedi wisdom and Starfleet commands to battle cries and running jokes. Answers can come from films or television, including franchises beyond those listed here.

provenance.brief: Name a famous quote or line from a space-based sci-fi film or TV series that fans still repeat.

May the Force be with you.reason: A widely quoted blessing spoken in multiple Star Wars films.

Live long and prosper.reason: Spock's iconic Vulcan farewell in Star Trek.

It's a trap!.reason: Admiral Ackbar says this during the Battle of Endor in Return of the Jedi.

Resistance is futile.reason: A recurring declaration by the Borg in Star Trek.

This is the way.reason: A recurring Mandalorian creed in The Mandalorian.

Never tell me the odds.reason: Han Solo says this to C-3PO in The Empire Strikes Back.

Make it so.reason: A signature command of Captain Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation.

Game over, man!.reason: Hudson exclaims this memorable line in Aliens.

Never give up, never surrender.reason: Commander Taggart's recurring catchphrase in Galaxy Quest.

By Grabthar's hammer.reason: Dr. Lazarus's recognizable oath in Galaxy Quest.

So say we all.reason: A recurring communal affirmation in the reimagined Battlestar Galactica.

I am a leaf on the wind.reason: Wash says this while piloting Serenity in the film Serenity.

I am your father.reason: Darth Vader says this to Luke in The Empire Strikes Back, preceded by 'No.'

I have a bad feeling about this.reason: This line and close variations recur throughout the Star Wars films.

Engage.reason: A recognizable command frequently spoken by Captain Picard in The Next Generation.

Open the pod bay doors, HAL.reason: Dave Bowman gives this instruction in 2001: A Space Odyssey.

There are four lights!.reason: Picard defiantly shouts this in The Next Generation episode 'Chain of Command, Part II.'

Nothing but the rain.reason: Starbuck gives this response to Adama's 'What do you hear?' in the reimagined Battlestar Galactica.

I am Groot.reason: Groot repeatedly speaks this signature phrase in the Guardians of the Galaxy films.

Smoke me a kipper.reason: Ace Rimmer's Red Dwarf catchphrase begins 'Smoke me a kipper, I'll be back for breakfast.'
